desc: The Savant path of zone intrusion has never run on a Jetson. Bring the stack up from docker-compose.l4t.yml with person_detection on for at least one real camera. Execute the 7-step checklist in docs/restricted-zones.md ("On a Jetson (not run yet)"), and fix the bugs it finds. title: Evaluate the engares model on our data
desc: The engares model has never been measured on our cameras. The reference reports 0.8466 for every metric of this checkpoint, including loss and AUC, so its evaluation is suspect. Using task 3, run it on: office test (task 1625), to compare with v5 AIRTLab hugs and high-fives, the play-fighting failure (v5 called 83.8% of them a fight) untrimmed ordinary footage, to measure false alarms per camera-hour

title: Export the streaming model for Jetson and verify parity
desc: Export the stream model with its state inputs and outputs to the Jetson runtime: TFLite first, or TensorRT if TFLite is too slow. The reference repository ships a model.tflite (39.5 MB). Check first what it is: which configuration, and whether it has stream states. Use it only if it matches the checkpoint chosen in task 4. The exported model must match TF frame by frame over a long stream, not just one clip.

title: Decision layer and per-camera threshold
desc: Turn the per-frame fight probability into alerts: smoothing, then k-of-n or hysteresis, a per-camera threshold, and a cooldown after each alert. Tune it on the task 4 data, aiming for the highest event recall at an agreed false-alarm budget per camera-hour.

title: Integrate the streaming model into the platform
desc: Re-add fighting to apps/platform using the exported stream model. Each camera keeps its own model state: states are created on connect, reset on reconnect or a gap in frames, and freed on disconnect, with a bounded number of cameras. Frames are sampled to the rate documented in task 3. Emit a fight event (declared in catalogue.yml emits), recorded with an evidence clip the same way as zone intrusion, and shown on the Events page. Product rules: action classification only, and no identity in the event.

title: Show the fight score in the AI preview
desc: In apps/platform/preview/render.py, show the live fight probability for the camera, for example a bar with a number, and highlight the frame border while an alert is active. Nothing identifies any person.

title: Jetson test, bug fixing and soak
desc: Run the full pipeline on the Jetson with several real cameras: camera, stream model, decision layer, event, clip, review queue. Fix the bugs found. Then run a soak test of at least 24 hours on ordinary footage to measure false alerts per camera-hour, throughput, thermals and restarts, and to confirm how many cameras one board can serve.

title: Decide the alarm catalogue and thresholds
desc: Define alarm types, and their respective conditions to trigger. Current default trigger condition for each alarm types (subject to change): Alarm type Raise Clear HighTemperature WARNING > 27 °C, CRITICAL > 30 °C < 26.5 °C LowTemperature WARNING < 20 °C > 20.5 °C HighHumidity WARNING > 70 % < 68 % LowHumidity WARNING < 35 % > 38 % LowBattery WARNING < 20 %, CRITICAL < 10 % >= 25 % DeviceOffline WARNING when `active` goes false `active` t rue Each raise condition must hold for 5 minutes before the alarm is raised. The offline timeout is measured, not assumed, as Aqara sensors report rarely.

title: Raise the low-battery alarm
desc: As the platform operator, I want an alarm when a sensor's battery runs low, so that the battery is replaced before the sensor goes silent. The rule applies to all profiles with battery.

title: Raise the offline alarm
desc: As the platform operator, I want an alarm when a device stops reporting, so that a dead sensor or gateway is noticed before its data is missed. A device is offline when ThingsBoard's `active` attribute goes false after the device's `inactivityTimeout`. That timeout is set per device and is not inherited by auto-created devices.

title: Show alarms on the room overview
desc: As a person looking at the room overview, I want open alarms shown per room and per device, so that I see a problem without opening ThingsBoard's alarm list.

Build a benchmark that puts PXP's existing intent corpus through the real classifier on both models and records the answer and the time taken for each case. Run it and compare: accuracy against the expected decision, and response time per call. Report the outcome.

title: Deploy Audio Scoring Service to Azure with scalable infrastructure
desc: Design the deployment architecture for the Audio Scoring Service: an asynchronous job model on Azure Container Apps, following the OCR service pattern. Write the infrastructure as code (Bicep) for the dev environment in the grader resource group. Deploy the infrastructure: storage (blob, table, queue), Container Apps environment, container registry, logging, and a Foundry resource for Speech (Southeast Asia). Rework the service to the asynchronous design: job API, queue worker with retries, Azure Storage, health checks and standard error responses. Add a Docker image and a test-gated deploy script. Deploy the service and verify end to end with a real recording.

title: [XT Parent] Install X-Tek, move to the xt-parent backend routes, and scope external-backend support
desc: Repo: xt-parent-ai ( develop ) | Depends on: 1734 ( xt-parent feat/1734-backend-factory ) | Estimate: 16h Background xt-parent-ai was forked from pxp-ai develop ( 5053be0 , PR 5274). It still calls the PXP backend paths under /api/dynamics . On feat/1734-backend-factory , xt-parent moved every one of those routes to the backend-neutral /xp/api/v1/... surface. There are no aliases, so the AI's current paths return 404 against the new backend. The mapping is in xt-parent/docs/1734-route-map.md . Scope 1. Install X-Tek (about 3h) Apply the X-Tek skeleton ( x-tek-cc ) using the Tier 2 python-fastapi example: docs/PROJECT-STANDARDS.md , project-context.md , CLAUDE.md , docs/TIER1-CONFORMANCE.md , .agents/skills/ . Merge with the existing CLAUDE.md , _bmad and .agents content instead of overwriting. Fill in TIER1-CONFORMANCE.md with the evidence that already exists (CI pipeline, Sonar, tests). 2. Update the AI to the new backend endpoints (about 9h) Change all 37 backend calls to their new paths (per docs/1734-route-map.md ). All go through service/api_client.py . Replace DYNAMICS_API_BASE_URL with a backend-neutral key (for example XT_PARENT_API_BASE_URL ) pointing at the /xp/api/v1 root. Update config.py and the Helm values. Remove the URL string hacks: .replace("/dynamics", "") ( policy_service.py:46,90 ), .replace('dynamics','external-apps') ( external_app_service.py:14 ), .replace('dynamics','parents') ( welcome_video_service.py:25 ). Method change: update-parent is sent as POST, but the route is PATCH /parents . Fix it or delete it (no agent calls it today). Update the tests and mocks that assert the old paths. Check the IEP downloadUrl pass-through against the new download paths ( cdf5dda ). 3. Investigate external-backend support (about 4h, output is a short doc + follow-up tickets) Answer: what must change so the AI works when xt-parent serves a tenant from a non-Dynamics (external) backend? Known points to confirm: - Tenant routing: the AI sends no tenant header. xt-parent takes the tenant from the token tid claim ( b5f03cf ) and refuses unmapped tenants (403/404) once BackendTenantMap:Tenants is set. Confirm the AI's forwarded token is enough for every flow, including background and A2A calls. - Dynamics-shaped payloads still in the AI: case creation ( case_service.py:30-40 ) sends CE fields ( CaseTitle , Customer , EmailParent ) with "Origin": "PXP" . The fee code reads F&O fields ( priceCurrencyCode , quantityUnitySymbol , pxpDisplay ). - Backend gaps in xt-parent: /students/cases has no neutral capability. PATCH /students still reads emergency contacts from Dynamics. Schools, policies, external-apps and topics are SQL-backed with no capability. The Odoo backend is not wired in yet ( d223c27 ). - No current OpenAPI spec for /xp/api/v1 ( docs/1734-pxp-openapi.json is pre-move). The AI needs one as its contract. - Confirm the AI targets xt-parent only, not xt-odoo directly (xt-odoo /xp/api/v1 is a different, CRUD-by-id API). Acceptance criteria X-Tek files are in the repo, and TIER1-CONFORMANCE.md is filled in with current evidence. No code in xt-parent-ai calls a /api/dynamics , CE/ , FNO/ or Nova path, and no code rewrites the base URL with string replace. The backend base URL comes from one backend-neutral config key, set in config.py and the Helm values. The unit tests pass. A smoke run against xt-parent feat/1734-backend-factory (dev) returns data for: attendance, timetable, events, fees due, school policy and welcome video. The investigation doc is in docs/ and lists each gap with an owner repo (xt-parent-ai or xt-parent). Follow-up tickets are created for it. Out of scope Rebranding pxp names (package name, Sonar key, pipeline, ACR, Helm chart, secret names, pxp_context ). This needs its own ticket, because renaming pxp_context changes checkpoint state keys. Fixing the backend gaps in xt-parent (they go to follow-up tickets). Risks The "wire shapes unchanged" claim comes from the 1734 commit messages plus a spot check, not a full JSON diff. The smoke run in AC 4 is the check. Blocked until feat/1734-backend-factory is deployed to a dev host.

title: Apply the XionTech design system to the va-edge operator app
desc: Goal Make the operator app (apps/platform/ui/web) look like the XionTech products by reusing @xiontech/design-system from xt-staff-fe (packages/design-system, v0.2.0) instead of its hand-written CSS, in a way that lets us take new design system versions quickly. How the package is consumed - The design system is not published to any registry. We pack it with `npm pack` and commit the tarball to va-edge: apps/platform/ui/web/vendor/xiontech-design-system-<version>.tgz - package.json depends on it as "file:vendor/xiontech-design-system-<version>.tgz". `npm ci` on a node needs no extra credentials. - Upgrade: pack the new version, `npm install` the new tarball, delete the old one, run the type check and tests, commit. - va-edge never edits design system code. A missing component or token is a PR to xt-staff-fe. - If an Azure Artifacts feed is set up later, only the dependency line changes. Scope Step 1 - tokens (whole app gets the XionTech look, markup unchanged) - Upgrade React 18 -> 19; add tailwindcss and @tailwindcss/vite. - Import @xiontech/design-system/styles.css; add @source for src/. - Theme switch: data-theme="xiontech" fixed, light/dark through data-mode. - Point the variables at the top of src/styles.css to design system role tokens (colour, font, radius, shadow). Video-specific tokens (zone, box, video overlay) stay local; the design system has none. - Keep the existing XionTechs logo (the pack's brand components are StaffXP's). Step 2 - components (replace the hand-written ones, delete their CSS) - Modal -> dialog, Hint -> tooltip, Loading -> spinner/skeleton, segmented control -> toggle-group, AccountMenu -> dropdown-menu, buttons and inputs -> button / input / field. Out of scope - Rewriting page layouts (Live, Events, Cameras, Node, Users) in Tailwind classes. - apps/video_wall/web and the static HTML demos. Risks to check first (spike, before step 1) - styles/index.css imports shadcn/tailwind.css but `shadcn` is a devDependency of the package: needs a small PR to xt-staff-fe, or va-edge installs `shadcn` itself. - @tailwindcss/vite on Vite 8 (xt-staff-fe runs Vite 7). - The package ships .ts source, so va-edge's strict tsc also checks its code. - .gitignore must not exclude vendor/ or *.tgz. - The package version must be bumped upstream on every change; record the source commit of the tarball in the web README. Acceptance criteria - `npm ci && npm run build` and `npm test` pass in apps/platform/ui/web. - `python apps/platform/check.py` passes; SonarQube gate stays green. - Light and dark mode both work on every tab and on the sign-in page. - The app builds and runs on a Jetson node through `va.py build`. - web/README.md documents the upgrade steps and the tarball's source commit. - scripts/check-contrast.mjs is reduced to the tokens that remain local, or removed.

title: SonarQube cleanup for xt-parent: fix the open findings on overall code
desc: The SonarQube project xt-parent ( dashboard ) fails its quality gate. The last analysis (2026-09-29) lists 108 open findings: 1 bug, 6 vulnerabilities, 79 code smells and 22 security hotspots, in 52 files. Goal Clear the open findings on the overall code, so the quality gate passes on develop . Scope In scope: C# in src/ and test/ , the payment HTML pages, Python scripts in scripts/ , Dockerfiles, docs, Sonar configuration. _bmad/ (installed BMad Method files, 18 findings): excluded from the scan, not edited. Security hotspots: fixed when a small, safe code change clears them; otherwise each one gets a written reason, and the owner marks it Safe in SonarQube. Out of scope: refactors and behaviour changes beyond what each finding needs. Approach Fetch the open issues and hotspots through the SonarQube Web API. Fix them on one branch from develop with the bmad-build workflow; one PR. Verify with the strict build ( XT_SECURITY_STRICT=1 , --no-incremental ), the tests, and a new SonarQube analysis. Acceptance criteria Every open finding is fixed, excluded with a reason, or listed as a reviewed hotspot with a reason. No new SonarQube finding, build warning or test failure. The quality gate of xt-parent passes after the PR is merged and develop is analysed.
